liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (2 reviews): The chimes in Dark Star come through crystal clear on this audience recording; The Truckin' into Dark Star, Main Ten, and Dancin' in the Streets sequence is called unique among shows [17][18]
- **The Main Ten** (1 review, 1 other source): Main Ten emerges from spacey Dark Star jams, then moves into a bouncing Dancin' jam driven by Billy and Mickey; Notes mark this as the final time The Main Ten was played [4][19]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): The electric set opens with a superb Morning Dew [19]
- **Dancin' In The Streets** (1 review): The reviewer calls the wild electric set one of the greatest ever [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Operator**: rare: 4 archived performances [24]
- **Wake Up Little Susie**: rare: 9 archived performances [24]
- **Mystery Train**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **My Babe**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **New Orleans**: rare: 5 archived performances [24]
- **Searchin'**: rare: 5 archived performances [24]
- **The Main Ten**: rare: 6 archived performances [24]
- **Dancin' Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Around And Around [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-11-08.aud.weiner.28609.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 43 songs; 268 min; rated 4.35/5 by 81 [1]. Said about its sound: For a vintage audience recording, it sounds notably good, though not at the level of 8/6/71 [23]
- **gd70-11-08.aud.owens.23474.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 45 songs; 240 min; rated 4/5 by 19 [2]. Said about its sound: Ambient crowd noise is heavy early on; reviewer suggests starting at Truckin'. Best on good headphones [17]
- **gd70-11-08.aud.warner.17184.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 44 songs; 241 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: This taping is a distorted mono mix, better as an archive than for listening; the other Nov. 8 tape is slightly better [15]
- **gd1970-11-08.aud.lee.pcrp.26975.shnf**: audience recording; 42 songs; 266 min; rated 5/5 by 22 [4]
- **gd1970-11-08.aud-weinberg.cousinit.18639.shnf**: audience recording; 32 songs; 171 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [6]. Said about its sound: The taper cut the very beginning of most songs to save tape [6]
- **gd1970-11-08.aud.garrett-evans.3339.shnf**: audience recording; 27 songs; 180 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says Pigpen and the whole band are on fire [21]
- Among 1970's many fantastic electric sets, this is one of the very best; Disc 4 rivals the 2/13/70 Dark Star segment [18]
- Last acoustic set until 1980; also final Operator, Wake Up Little Susie, and acoustic Uncle John's Band [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-11-08.aud.weiner.28609.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Ken & Judy Lee; transferred by Noah Weiner; source: Audience - Ken & Judy Lee [1]. Also: This is a patched fix of the latest upgrade, circulated by The Port Chester Resurrection Project [1]
- **gd70-11-08.aud.owens.23474.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Ken Lee and Marty Weinberg; transferred by The Wizard; source: Audience [2]. Also: Reviewer notes that soundboards of this show and 6/24/70 are sought after, and Owsley was in jail then [14]
- **gd70-11-08.aud.warner.17184.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Marty Weinberg and Ken Lee; transferred by Jack Warner; source: Audience - Marty Weinberg and Ken Lee [3]
- **gd1970-11-08.aud.lee.pcrp.26975.shnf**: taped by Ken and Judy Lee; transferred by PCRP; source: See info file [4]. Also: A release from Ken and Judy Lee, dedicated to Mark Cohen on the second anniversary of his death [4]
- **gd1970-11-08.aud-weinberg.cousinit.18639.shnf**: transferred by CousinIt; source: MAR source seems to be from Marty Weinberg's master, recorded from the floor, AKG 190E mic > Uher 4000 Report-L 5" reel machine. [6]. Also: Morning Dew and Dancin' segments come from Ken Leigh's master; the Dancin' through Good Lovin' ending comes from Marty Weinberg's master; The acoustic set was on an old Ampex tape that kept dragging and stopping the cassette; it was restored incrementally [6]
- **gd1970-11-08.aud.garrett-evans.3339.shnf**: transferred by Miles Garrett and Morgan Evans; source: Audience [7]. Also: A composite of mixed generations; Miles Garrett did the DAT to CD conversion and Morgan Evans the CD to SHN; Composite of one audience source patched with a second; the final reel is a higher-generation copy of the first source [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Richard Biffle Art: [Grateful Dead" Capitol Theatre 11/08/1970 | Richard Biffle Art](https://www.richardbiffleart.com/product-page/grateful-dead-capitol-theatre-11-08-1970) [25]
- Fan art by Richard Biffle Screen-Printed: [Painter and Illustrator | Olcrowstudio](https://www.olcrowstudio.com/) [26]
